_: phase_1/translate.py — every knob, at its default, with the reason beside it. Nothing about the provider, the corpus or the prompt is hardcoded in translate.py. --config points elsewhere; CLI flags override individual keys. Paths are relative to phase_1/.

corpus._: The clause set. modelspec_clauses.json is the segmentation of record: 593 clauses, each with id, quote, section_id, section_path, kind, locator.
corpus._description: What the corpus IS, one line, rendered into the USER block. It belongs there and not in the system block: the system block is the METHOD of translation and should be byte-identical across corpora, which also keeps it cacheable. A corpus-specific sentence in it makes the prompt fit only the document it was written for.
corpus.description: a behavioural specification for an AI assistant

select._: What to translate. A clause id list wins over section; section wins over kind. All three empty = refuse, because 'translate everything' is not a thing to do by accident.
select._kinds: modelspec_kinds over 410 classified clauses: conditional 188, definitional 84, meta 72, holistic 66. `definitional` clauses emit facts and are the easy end of stage 1; `conditional` clauses are the ones that need rules.

cross_references._: 03_pipeline.md: 'a clause that modifies rules defined elsewhere cannot be translated in isolation'. The spec carries its own cross-references as markdown anchors — [restricted](#restricted_content) — and section_id values match those anchors. link.py measured 45 of 46 distinct targets resolving.
cross_references._lower_bound: ⚠️ Only ~13% of clauses carry anchors, so this is a LOWER BOUND on dependencies, never the whole set. A clause with no anchors is not thereby dependency-free.

prompt._: The translation rules live in these files, not in the code, so they can be edited and diffed on their own. Concatenated in the order listed to form the SYSTEM block — which is identical for every clause and is therefore the cacheable prefix.
prompt._order: 03_pipeline.md: everything repeated first, everything that varies last. The clause text and its cross-references go in the USER block.
prompt._orphan_guard: Every .md in prompt/ must appear here or in unused_files. A prompt file that exists and is never sent is the pass-looks-like-did-not-run failure in prompt form — it happened once already with 30_failure_modes.md. A self-test enforces this.

model._: TWO MODES. If `model` and `base_url` are both set, the provider is defined INLINE here and providers.json is not consulted for it. Otherwise `provider_name` must name a row in providers.json. A name that matches nothing, with no inline model, RAISES — a typo must never fall through to some default model.
model._inline_why: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is not a row in providers.json, and providers.json belongs to the wider repo. Defining it here keeps the change inside walkthrough/, which is where it belongs.
model._model: VERIFIED 2026-08-07 against together.ai/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731: the model id is `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, context 1M. `--list-models` re-checks it against the live catalogue before spending.
model._price_per_mtok: [$/Mtok input, $/Mtok output]. SOURCE: together.ai model page, fetched 2026-08-07 — $0.14 in, $0.28 out, $0.03 cached input. Cached input is NOT claimed here: the estimate bills every input token at the full rate, which is the conservative direction and is what a hard $8.50 ledger cap deserves.
model._format_forcing: json_schema | json_object | none. json_schema is what 03_pipeline.md stage 1 means by 'format-forced ... guaranteed at generation rather than checked afterwards'. VERIFIED 2026-08-07 from docs.together.ai/docs/json-mode that together.ai accepts exactly {type: json_schema, json_schema: {name, schema}} — the shape this harness sends. STILL UNVERIFIED: that THIS model is on the supported list (the catalogue examples are Qwen and Llama), and whether `strict` is honoured. The first live call is the test; a 400 mentioning response_format means fall back to json_object and RECORD the departure from stage 1.
model._json_schema_strict: together.ai's docs do not document a `strict` key. Sending an unknown key may be ignored or may 400. Set false to drop it.
model._max_tokens: This is a REASONING model (together.ai recommends up to 384K output at high reasoning effort). Hidden reasoning is billed as output and can dominate. 16384 is generous for one module; if a completion comes back truncated the harness RAISES rather than writing half a module, so the failure is loud.

output._: One directory per run. The raw response is always written before any parsing, so a parse failure never loses what was paid for.

cost._: Estimate printed BEFORE any call and gated. Over the ceiling, nothing is sent. An unpriced provider counts as OVER budget, never as free.
cost._assumed_output_tokens: Deliberately the full max_tokens, i.e. the worst case, not the ~600 tokens a module costs. Overstating an estimate is survivable; understating is how a hard cap gets passed.

repair._: Stage 2's repair loop. A failing translation is sent back in ONE accumulating transcript carrying its own prior modules and every check they failed, with reasons. Only stage-2 findings may enter it; later stages carry expected answers and are filtered by origin.
repair._max_attempts: 1 disables repair entirely. The cost gate prices the budget: input grows with the transcript, so the estimate is triangular in the attempt count, not linear.

graveyard._: Where a clause goes when repair does not converge — and some that do. A non-converging clause carries a signal about the PROMPT, not only about that clause, and it is only visible by comparing entries against each other.
graveyard._rates: Failures, flagged repairs and last-attempt successes are ALWAYS kept. These rates cover the rest. `first_try` is deliberately non-zero: a graveyard holding only trouble makes every diagnosis read as 'the prompt is broken', and a diagnosing agent needs cases where it worked. Sampling is a hash of the clause id, so two runs over one corpus keep the same population.
graveyard._cap: Reaching it REFUSES to start another run. A hundred uninspected non-convergences is not a corpus; it is one defect recorded a hundred times, and the rest of the budget spent reproducing it.
